Shadowing occurs when a local variable or constructor parameter has the same name as an instance variable.
For example:

6. What is a copy constructor in Java?
A copy constructor is a constructor that accepts an object of the
same class type
as its parameter.
It is used to create a new object by copying values from an existing object.
For example:
The copy constructor is:

runs.text: The parameter s is of the same type as the class, Student.
An object can be copied as follows:

blocks.text:
Student s1 = new Student(101);
Student s2 = new Student(s1);

runs.text: Here, the values of s1 are copied into s2.
7. What are the six static and instance elements of a Java class?
A class can contain the following six static and instance elements:
1. Static variable
2. Static block
3. Static method
4. Instance variable
5. Instance block
6. Instance method
A constructor is also an important member associated with object creation and initialization.
8. Which members can access static and instance variables?
The access relationship can be summarized as follows:
A static member can directly access another static member because both belong to the class.
An instance member can access both static and instance members because it executes in the context of an object.
A static block cannot directly access an instance variable because an instance variable belongs to an object, while the static block executes when the class is loaded, before an object is created.
9. Why can a static block not directly access an instance variable?
A static block is executed when the class is loaded.
At that stage, an object may not have been created yet. Instance variables receive their memory when an object is created.
The execution sequence is therefore:

blocks.text:
Class loading
                ↓
 Static elements are initialized
                ↓
      Static block executes
                ↓
         main() executes
                ↓
      Object may be created
                ↓
Instance variables receive memory

runs.text: Since an instance variable does not belong to the class itself and an object may not yet exist when the static block executes, the static block cannot directly access that instance variable.
10. In what order are static block, static method, instance block, constructor, and instance method executed?
Consider a class containing all these elements:
If the application contains:
The execution order is:
Static block executed
Static method executed
Instance block executed
Constructor executed
Instance method executed

The static block executes during class loading. The static method is then called without creating an object. When the object is created, the instance block executes before the constructor. Finally, the instance method executes when it is called.
11. Does the position of an instance block and constructor in the class change their execution order?
No. The position of the constructor and instance block in the source code does not change their execution order during object creation.
When an object is created:

blocks.text:
Instance block
      ↓
Constructor

runs.text: The instance block executes before the constructor.
Therefore, moving the constructor above the instance block in the source code does not make the constructor execute first.
12. What is the difference between an instance block and a constructor?
Both can be used for initializing instance variables, but they are used for different purposes.
Consider a
Student
class having:
name
id
gender
maritalStatus
Suppose name, id, and gender are different for every student, while
maritalStatus
should initially be false for every student.
The constructor can initialize values that are specific to each object:
The instance block can initialize a value that should receive the same initial value whenever an object is created:
Thus:
Object-specific values → Constructor
Common initial instance values → Instance block
The constructor receives object-specific values through parameters, whereas the instance block executes automatically whenever an object is created.
13. When should a variable be declared as static?
A variable should be declared as static when its value is
common to all objects of the class
For example, the value of PI is common when calculating the area of different shapes.
The same value can be used by objects representing different shapes.
Another example is nationality when every object represents a person with the same nationality:

blocks.text: static String nationality = "Indian";

runs.text: The important rule is:
Value common to all objects → static variable
Value specific to an
object  →
instance variable
14. How can the number of objects
created
for a class be counted?
A static variable can be used to maintain the count because the count must be common to all objects.
The constructor can increment the count whenever an object is created.
Output:
The variable count is static, so only one common copy is maintained for the class. Every time the constructor executes, count is incremented.
The static variable should be accessed using the class name:

blocks.text: Demo.count

runs.text: rather than through an object reference.
15. What is a Singleton design pattern?
A Singleton design pattern is a predefined set of rules used to ensure that only
one object of a class
is created.
The three main rules given for the Singleton implementation are:
1. Make the constructor private.
2. Create a private static reference variable to hold the object reference.
3. Provide a public static method that creates and returns the object

blocks.text: if it does not already exist, or returns the existing object.

runs.text: The private constructor prevents code outside the class from directly creating objects.
The static reference stores the single object reference and can be accessed by the static method.
16. How is the
ChiefMinister
class converted into a Singleton class?
Suppose the class contains a name, term, and constructor:
To convert it into a Singleton class, the constructor is made private and a private static reference is created.
The object is obtained through the static method:

blocks.text: ChiefMinister cm = ChiefMinister.getInstance("ABC", 10);

runs.text: The constructor cannot be called directly from outside the class:

blocks.text: ChiefMinister cm = new ChiefMinister("ABC", 10);

runs.text: because the constructor is private.
If the object already exists,
getInstance
) returns the existing reference instead of creating another object.
